questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study creative writing and uni of Southampton was one of the few bachelor programs with a lot of different possibilities in these modules.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been an amazing experience and I would recommend it to all.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Once I came everything seemed very intuitive and there was plenty of help to find both in my accommodation and at the university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The people in my accommodation was ready to help with my things. 
Within the first days I received a lot of information from the uni. There was also many different activities to participate in.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in a university accommodation in the city center. It was easy to apply for the different types before going and I received my offer of housing about a month before arriving.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: It was possible to have catered packages including lunch and snacks at uni, but I didn't use this since it was quit expensive and I had a fine shared kitchen in my flat.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky to have nice and clean flatmates, but my experience is that many had to deal with both a lot of noise and mess. However, I think it is a great way of getting to know more people than the ones you study with.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a very long proces and not everyone got what they wanted, but I was happy with the modules I got in the end.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I first had to send an application with different information. After this I had to apply for modules. Then there was another registration round with more details. When I arrived I had to make my final choice of modules.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was different emails you could write to with questions depending on what you wanted help with.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was successful since I got to have two creative writing modules and one module with the possibility to write a lot of creative work. However, some of the modules I had looked at from home were no longer available.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be too disappointed if they don't offer exactly the modules you wanted in the first place - but do all you can to get into the ones you want. I had to talk to my tutors and not just apply online to be sure to get what I wanted.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I went on exchange on my fifth semester and took BA-level courses. I found the level to be appropriate since it was in english.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think it was quit similar - though the length of the lessons were a lot different. At uni of Southampton most of my lessons were only 45 minutes long.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
A Stranger Comes to Town - Introduction to creative writing

The Act of the Essay

Writing the Novel

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Writing the Novel for anyone who wants to write. It was very useful.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I spend a lot of money on train journeys to cities nearby to experience the area - this was really great. 
I had a free bus pass, so I didn't spend money on transport within the city.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I think most things were of similar price as it is in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined many societies and there was so many to choose from.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a club or society for almost everything and in the first week there was a fair where you could talk to people from the different clubs and decide from there.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the Hill Walking Society. This was a great way of exploring the area with a free guide in the beautiful nature.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips! Southampton is great for studying but there are plenty of must see attractions; Stonehenge, New Forrest, Isle of Wight and cities nearby; Winchester, Brighton, Bath, Bristol, London.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy ;)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I think the societies is a good place to meet people, but also through the meetings with the other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love the politeness and friendliness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Remember to find a balance between study time and adventure time - there is room for both and there should be.

Go away in the weekends - experience as much as possible.

Don't stress - you will find friends and you will do a lot of cool stuff.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Know that they are easy to communicate with and remember to ask whenever there is something you are not sure about - they are happy to help.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To experience the country and to have an everyday here.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To find time for everything I wanted.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go - you won't regret it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
